scope: Proposition 8.3 (Holomorphic comparison) of the manuscript “The height-three chromatic overlap: an explicit filtration and its attachments” (preprints/The-height-three-chromatic-overlap-an-explicit-filtration-and-its-attachments-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 05577ee22db5cad1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 67. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every specified coefficient line the natural map RΓcts(G, Bhol(L)) −→ RΓcts(G, Bpk(L)) is a quasi-isomorphism. Its cohomology groups are finite, and the chosen Frobenius power acts invertibly on them. For a profinite parameter space T, the comparison and Frobenius invertibility persist, and the cohomology is naturally C T, Ha cts(G, Bhol(L))  , where the finite point-value cohomology group has its discrete topology. Finiteness is asserted for the cohomology without parameters. The comparison is compatible with coefficient-field descent. For the untwisted line it identifies the natural constants comparison of Proposition 5.9.
